questions.q: A patient is at risk of falling. What helps prevent a fall?
options: Bed at its highest so they can get up easily
Room fully dark so they sleep well
Bed low, wheels locked, call bell within reach
Tell them to walk alone to build strength

questions.q: Which protective item keeps blood off your hands?
A patient refuses to take a medicine. What do you do?
options: Ask why, inform the doctor and record it
Throw it away and say nothing

questions.q: Where do you check the radial pulse?
options: At the side of the neck
At the wrist, on the thumb side

questions.q: You find a patient who does not respond when you call and tap them. What do you do first?
options: Give them a sip of water
Go to fetch their file first
Shout for help and check breathing

questions.q: Why do you raise the head of the bed when a patient is eating?
options: To lower the risk of choking

questions.q: The doctor's written order is hard to read. What do you do?
options: Give the dose you think is likely
Clarify it with the doctor before giving
Skip the dose and tell no one
Ask the patient what dose they take

questions.q: Staff are caring for a patient with suspected lung TB. Which mask should they wear?
What is the main reason for a proper handover at the change of shift?
options: So the next nurse knows each patient's needs
So the shift can end a little early

questions.q: Before measuring blood pressure, the patient should…
By which route is insulin usually given on the ward?
A patient hasn't passed urine for 8 hours after surgery. What do you do?
options: Check for a full bladder and tell the doctor
Give a painkiller and leave it

questions.q: Soon after a new IV antibiotic starts, a patient gets itching, a rash and breathlessness. What do you do first?
options: Slow the drip and watch for an hour
Stop the infusion and call the doctor urgently

questions.q: The order is 1 g. The vial has 500 mg in 2 ml. How much do you draw up?
In adult CPR, how deep should chest compressions be?
You get a needle-stick injury from a used needle. What is the first step?
options: Wash with soap and running water, then report at once
Squeeze hard and suck the wound
Ignore it if the wound is small

questions.q: A diabetic patient's blood sugar is 54 mg/dL. They are awake and can swallow. What do you do first?
options: Give quick sugar like glucose, recheck in 15 minutes

questions.q: After surgery, a patient's pulse rises from 80 to 120 and BP falls to 90/60. What might this mean?
options: Possible bleeding or shock: tell the doctor at once

questions.q: Two patients with the same name are in one ward. What prevents a medicine mix-up?
options: Go by the bed number only
Call the name aloud and wait
Check two identifiers and the ID band each time
Ask the relatives which patient it is

task.title: Write a shift handover for a patient who is getting worse
task.brief: Take about 20 minutes. Read the patient's notes below. Write a short handover (about 150–250 words) for the next nurse, in SBAR order: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. Point out which findings are worrying and what should be done now. A good answer is accurate, picks out every warning sign, says the doctor must be told now (not at the next round), and is clear and safe.
task.material:
Patient: Ramesh Iyer, 62, Bed 14, surgical ward. Day 1 after hernia surgery.
History: type 2 diabetes, on insulin. Allergy: penicillin.
2 pm: Temp 37.2 °C, pulse 84, BP 128/80, breathing 18/min, SpO2 97%. Pain 3/10.
6 pm: Temp 38.4 °C, pulse 108, BP 104/68, breathing 22/min, SpO2 94%. Pain 6/10.
Last painkiller: 1 pm.
Urine: 150 ml since 10 am.
Blood sugar at 6 pm: 248 mg/dL.
Wound dressing: small spot of blood at 2 pm; larger, spreading stain at 6 pm.
Doctor informed of the 6 pm findings: not yet.
key_points: Notes the new fever, faster pulse and breathing, lower BP and SpO2
Notes low urine output since 10 am
Notes the spreading blood on the dressing
Notes high blood sugar and the diabetes history
Says the doctor must be informed now and observations repeated often
Mentions pain score and that pain relief is due as prescribed

rubric.label: Accurate and safe
rubric.guide: 0 = wrong facts or unsafe advice, 3 = facts right but misses the urgency, 5 = accurate, safe and says to inform the doctor now

rubric.label: Warning signs found
rubric.guide: 0 = one sign noted, 3 = about half the warning signs, 5 = vitals, urine, wound, sugar and allergy all covered

rubric.label: SBAR structure
rubric.guide: 0 = no order, 3 = partly in SBAR, 5 = clear Situation, Background, Assessment and Recommendation

rubric.label: Clarity
rubric.guide: 0 = hard to follow, 3 = clear but long or vague, 5 = short, clear sentences the next nurse can act on
